To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The leading non-universal analytic corrections to universal asymptotically free scaling, for all choices of lattice actions, are given by the 2-loop perturbative expansion of the renormalized coupling, and (ii) the actual scaling violations observed in lattice Monte Carlo simulations are due to non-analytic, non-perturbatively generated corrections.

(i) the 1-loop and 2-loop perturbative corrections to universal scaling are in excellent agreement with Monte Carlo simulations; (ii) the 3-loop corrections are in fair agreement, but the deviations from universal scaling observed in Monte Carlo simulations are not explained by the 3-loop perturbative analytic terms; (iii) the 3-loops ratios of scaling operators over Λ-parameters are in excellent agreement, but the 2-loops ratios are not.

the non-perturbatively renormalized non-linear sigma model, for a wide class of lattice actions, is asymptotically free; the leading non-universal corrections to universal scaling are perturbative, and are known up to three-loop order; the actual deviations from asymptotic scaling are non-perturbativel and are not due to the lattice regularization, but to the presence of the continuum cutoff.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the asymptotic scaling of the non-linear σ model on the lattice.
the study of the non-linear sigma model on the lattice, and in particular with its renormalization group properties.
a detailed study of the perturbative and non-perturbatve renormalization of the non-linear σ model on a lattice, and its implications for Monte Carlo simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
perturbative renormalization group theory is not sufficient to describe the non-linear σ model in the scaling region.
, while the non-universal terms are important to understand the lattice renormalization, the universal terms are not, and that the latter are not even needed to determine the ratios.
perturbative calculations of renormalization functions and Monte Carlo simulations of the non-linear σ model are in agreement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lattice scaling of the σ-model is very well understood.
the perturbative approach is not sufficient to describe the non-linear σ model on a lattice, but it provides the necessary ingredients to describe the model in the continuum.
the non-perturbatively improved σ-model, with a suitable choice of the lattice action, has the best scaling properties of all lattice regularized theories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perturbative approach can provide a useful tool to disentangle the various effects at play in lattice simulations.

, while the perturbative renormalization is a necessary step in order to understand the non-perturbatively computed scaling functions, the actual scaling functions are dominated by non-perturbate effects, and are not directly related to the perturbative expansion.
, in the continuum limit, the perturbative corrections to the renormalization-group functions are not the main source of non-universal scaling corrections.
